messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — users started flagging p99 regressions for sparrow-13b-v2 about 35 minutes after we rolled the tokenizer normalization patch.
Jake Peters: Confirmed on our dashboards. p95 steady around 430ms, p99 jumped from ~460ms -> ~2.1s for requests with >16k tokens.
Liu Wang: Which deploy/PR rolled?
Maya Chen: Roll was at 2123456000 — PR #4902 (tokenizer: unicode-normalizer + bpe-split-adjust). Commit c2b1f7d. Canary looked fine with short prompts.
Anna Rodriguez: p95 unchanged suggests tail cases. Could be a KV cache cold-path or extra tokenize passes.
Jake Peters: I pulled a trace, long time is in tokenizer.normalize() and kvcache.lock wait. Snippet: 
``
span tokenizer.normalize -> 610ms
span kvcache.lookup    -> 940ms
span model.forward     -> 210ms
```
Maya Chen: Repro steps I ran: 
1) curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"sparrow-13b-v2","inputs":"<~19k token prompt>"}'
2) header X-Redwood-Route: hosted
3) run 6x to check cold vs warm
Result: first three calls p99 ~2.0s, then drops to ~480ms after warm KV.
Rick O'Neill: Likely combo of token inflation + cold KV misses.
Liu Wang: Can we diff token counts between v1 and v2? Also any looped normalization for mixed-language tokens?
Maya Chen: Diffed outputs: v2 typically emits +9% tokens for certain unicode-heavy prompts due to extra NFKC normalizer path and additional merge-safeguard. Also observed re-tokenization when punctuation+emoji combos present.
Anna Rodriguez: 9% more tokens at high lengths explains a lot — KV lookups and attention memory scale non-linearly for tails.
infra-bot: Deploy event: PR #4902 merged by maya@redwood at 2123456000. Canary verdict: pass for 200 short-context requests. Full rollout at 2123457800.
Jake Peters: Mitigation options on the table: 
- immediate rollback of tokenizer PR
- backport a short-circuit in normalizer for long sequences
- route long-context users to sparrow-13b-v1 or a long-seq-optimized variant
- bump KV cache size per-worker as a temporary shield (costly)
Maya Chen: We've staged a rollback if hotfix doesn't stabilize — targeted rollback time 2123460000.
Liu Wang: Quick runtime mitigation idea: if seq_estimate > 13k, flip to fast-normalizer which skips expensive unicode passes. Gate via model config flag. Low-risk to push.
Anna Rodriguez: Support: notify affected customers (cust-734, cust-801, cust-912) with guidance to avoid >12k tokens or request dedicated routing.
Jake Peters: I made a canary patch: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/commit/9d4f2ab. Patch adds: 
``
if (seq_est > 13000) {
  normalizer.mode = FAST;
}
```
Maya Chen: Canary (5% traffic) metrics after enabling FAST normalizer: p95 470ms, p99 560ms for long-context. Good sign.
Rick O'Neill: Note tradeoff — FAST normalizer bypasses some edge-case unicode folding; we need to quantify possible generation differences.
Liu Wang: We'll gate FAST via runtime flag and A/B it on a subset of customers. I'll own rollback PR and fast-normalizer gate. ETA 45m.
Anna Rodriguez: Draft communication for support: "We're investigating increased latency for long-context requests after a tokenizer update. Temporary mitigations: reduce prompt length (<12k tokens) or route to dedicated pools. We're deploying a partial hotfix now and will rollback if issues persist."
Jake Peters: Added logs to the support ticket: 
``
[2123458032] req_id=xyz123 seq_est=17610 token_inflation=1.09 tokenizer_time=612ms kvcache_miss=true
[2123458048] req_id=opq456 seq_est=18340 token_inflation=1.11 tokenizer_time=638ms kvcache_miss=true
```
Rick O'Neill: Also flag billing impact: ~9% token inflation => cost increase for these windows. Finance will want an estimate and decide on credits.
Anna Rodriguez: I'll prepare a bill-impact calc and the message for customers by EOD.
Maya Chen: Action items summary: 
- Liu: rollback PR + fast-normalizer gate (45m)
- Jake: add tokenizer inflation metric + tokenizer latency histograms by length (2h)
- Anna: customer comms + billing impact estimate (1h)
- Rick: monitor canary and set auto-rollback if error rate or latency worsens (30m)
Ticket created: SUP-99801. Add to incident board if >4 customers impacted.
infra-bot: Fast-normalizer canary applied to 5% traffic at 2123458200 by maya@redwood
Maya Chen: Canary after 20m: stable, p99 for long-context down to ~580ms. Increasing canary to 25%.
Liu Wang: Opening PR to revert full tokenizer change if we need it: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/4923
Jake Peters: Also queued an eval run to compare quality across the long-context prompt set — run-id eval-212345-2
Anna Rodriguez: Support notified customers listed and applied routing changes for those with Dedicated. Ticket updated SUP-99801.
Maya Chen: Thanks all. Will update if rollback required. :thumbsup:
